summary: IDS s127_double is degraded: 4.2% of frames are dropped as oversize (>1518B) and 28.6% are opaque inside ERSPAN tunnels, both reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo/encapsulated frames up to 8108 bytes to a 1Gbps IDS port with 1518-byte MTU. 142/3381 frames (4.2%) exceed the NIC limit and are dropped in hardware.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS silently misses 4.2% of traffic, including large frames that often carry data exfiltration or exploit payloads; with needs_full_payload=true detection is blind to those flows.

recommended_fix.why: Tool requires full payload so broker slicing/trimming to 1518B is not an option. Increase IDS NIC and broker egress MTU to jumbo (9000-9216) or reduce upstream MTU to prevent NIC drops without payload loss.

findings.root_cause: 28.6% of traffic (968/3381 frames) arrives encapsulated in ERSPAN. Broker is forwarding tunnel-encapsulated frames without decapsulation/stripping.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer ERSPAN/IP/GRE headers, not inner Ethernet/IP and L7 payload, so signatures and anomaly detection cannot fire on 28.6% of traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker exposes inner frames to the IDS, restoring full L2-L7 inspection without requiring IDS to decode tunnels.
